name: service_latency
supersedes: protocol-v4.json (all v3 rules incl. addenda stay in force: composition-exact gate via the converter's operation_classes(), harness classes constant across U / K (max - min <= 2), single / pair derivation, N_unit divisor, b300 10 % control rule, independent crediting of lat (result / completion) and thr (issue_interval) per class); v5 adds cells for the v4 leftovers and two explicitly declared rules (NOP filler, CS2R windows)
corpus: executed warp instructions in the 450 x 2 single-cluster facts ($A/diag/mb4/dyncount-{hp,bw}.tsv): CS2R.CLOCK and CS2R.GLOBALTIMER 4952 each in 168 h100 cases, none on b300; HFMA2 h100 4700 / 14 cases; DMUL 286 / 18 and DSETP 408 / 17 (h100), 100 / 5 each (b300); DADD 0 on both; MATCH 1 (h100 flashinfer_batch_decode_paged_03, MATCH.ANY R2, R3, 8 distinct captured source values).

cells.CS2R_CLOCK: both devices, issue only. K in {16, 32, 64} back-to-back mov.u64 %0, %clock64 in asm volatile: the first read is t_first, the last t_last, the K - 2 middle reads write one scratch register that is never read (no accumulation, so nothing else per step); window = t_last - t_first (K - 1 intervals); interval = OLS slope of the window over K. Gate (special window rule): between the first and the last read exactly K instructions of class CS2R.CLOCK (the 64-bit corpus form CS2R Rd, SR_CLOCKLO; S2UR / CS2R.32 forms do not count) and nothing whose count scales with K. Credited to CS2R.CLOCK issue_interval_cycles.
cells.CS2R_GT: both devices, issue only. t0 = clock64; K in {16, 32, 64} back-to-back mov.u64 %0, %globaltimer (all but the last into one never-read scratch register, the last folded into a sink after t1); t1 = clock64; window = t1 - t0 in SM cycles (the v4 cell timed the window in globaltimer units, 32 ns ticks on H100, which cannot give cycles). Gate: between the two clock reads exactly K instructions of class CS2R.GLOBALTIMER (64-bit CS2R Rd, SR_GLOBALTIMERLO form) and nothing that scales with K. Interval = OLS slope over K. Credited to CS2R.GLOBALTIMER issue_interval_cycles.
cells.HFMA2: h100 only: the v4 lat and thr cells unchanged in body, thr K extended to {16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128}; the model records per kernel the HFMA2 / HFMA2.MMA split (both are class HFMA2). lat and thr are credited independently (v3 rule). thr: v3 acceptance on the OLS slope over all K; if the residual exceeds 5 % the interval is unrealised:nonlinear and the per-K per-instruction rates are reported (no K subset is selected).
cells.DADD_DMUL_RN: both devices: compile-only survey first (tools/microbench/service_latency/survey, no timing) of this ordered idiom list for a lat chain and an 8-chain thr body: (1) add.rn.f64 x, x, y; (2) sub.rn.f64 x, x, y; (3) mul.rn.f64 x, x, y; (4) mul.f64 x, x, y; (5) add.rn.f64 x, x, y with y = neg(y) loaded once before the window. For DADD the cell is the first of (1), (2), (5) whose SASS on that device passes the composition-exact gate with composition {DADD: 1} (no rounding suffix, i.e. the corpus form); for DMUL the first of (3), (4) with {DMUL: 1}. The survey verdict is written to $A/microbench/service_latency/survey/<device>-svy7 before the GPU run; a class with no passing idiom on a device stays unrealised:contracted and is not timed. Timed cells: lat U in {16, 32, 64}, dthr K in {16, 32, 64}; credited to DADD / DMUL; a passing value replaces the .RZ-derived experimental value (v4) and is measured if it passes the v3 acceptance.
cells.FP64_b300: b300 DADD_RZ, DMUL_RZ, DSETP_P (v4 bodies unchanged) and the DADD_DMUL_RN cells if realised, under the NOP filler rule below.
cells.MATCH: both devices: match.any.sync.b32 with d distinct values among the 32 lanes, d in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32} (lane value = seed + (lane % d)); lat: one dependent chain (the result mask feeds the next MATCH, which keeps the distinct count at d: lanes of one group share one mask), U in {16, 32, 64}; thr: 8 independent chains with the same d, K in {16, 32, 64}. Per d: result(d) = lat slope, interval(d) = thr slope / per-unit divisor (v3 N_unit rule, match_smsp).
cells.MATCH_model: result and interval as functions of d: if an affine fit a + b x d over the six d has max relative residual <= 5 % on both runs, the leaf fields become affine(match_distinct_values); otherwise linear knots on match_distinct_values at the six d (interpolated between, clamped outside). Requires the converter axis below; the b300 values 105 / 64.0 (blackwell-prototype w5, distinct count of that probe unknown) are reported against the curve, not used as a control.

nop_filler_rule: sm_103a ptxas follows every FP64 instruction of these cells with a fixed run of NOPs whose control words carry stall counts (4 NOPs per DADD / DMUL in the v4 b300 SASS, lat and thr alike). NOP is then allowed in the window when its count per target instruction is the same integer for every U / K (exact proportionality; otherwise the gate fails as in v3). Let S = the sum of the stall counts of one step's NOPs plus the target instruction's own stall count, read from the SASS control words (sass_ctrl.py). lat: result = slope, credited only if slope >= S + 2 cycles on both runs (the dependency, not the compiler's fixed stall schedule, sets the step); else unrealised:stall_bound. thr: interval = slope per target instruction - n_NOP x 1 cycle (the engine issues each NOP in one slot with no stall), credited only if the per-instruction slope >= S + 2; else unrealised:stall_bound. Status cap experimental for every value credited under this rule; pair cells (DSETP) subtract the partner as in v3 after this rule.
converter_axis: new capture axis match_distinct_values (unit count, owner capture): for an instruction of class MATCH, the number of distinct values of its source register over the executing lanes, read from the instruction's own captured lane values (MATCH is in the tracer's operand-capture family); .U64 forms use the (Rn, Rn+1) pair; a value not captured -> missing_fact:axis:match_distinct_values; NOT_APPLICABLE for every other class. python (python/cyclescope/convert/axes.py) and cpp (cpp/convert/axes.cpp) identical, with a pytest on a synthetic MATCH record and a py == cpp check on the corpus case. The axis and the MATCH leaf's axis use are a semantic commit; leaf values come from this protocol's run only.
gate: v3 composition-exact gate with the harness scaling check (sass_check_alu5.py extended or a new sass_check_alu6.py); CS2R cells use the special window rules above; FP64 b300 cells use the NOP filler rule.
acceptance: v3 verbatim (single: residual <= 5 % and two runs <= 5 % -> measured; pair: capped experimental; b300 control 10 % rule for classes with an installed measured leaf).
install: v3 install rules (sources service_latency.<device>.v5r<n>[.experimental]); unrealised cells leave their leaves untouched with the reason recorded in docs/en/microbench.md; A/B 500 x 2 single-cluster against the current main baseline.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or derivation change after data; no idiom search after data (the DADD / DMUL idiom is fixed by the compile-only survey before any timing)

addenda.text: Correction of converter_axis (written before any timing of this protocol): the capture axis match_distinct_values already exists (common/axes.json; python axes.py _f_match_distinct_values, cpp axes.cpp f_match_distinct) but counts the distinct values of whichever captured register comes first. On the only corpus MATCH (flashinfer_batch_decode_paged_03, MATCH.ANY R2, R3) the operand capture holds both R2 (the destination's pre-execution value) and R3 (the source); the axis reads R2. Fix (semantic converter commit, python and cpp identical): the axis reads the instruction's first source register (static source_registers[0]; for .U64 forms the pair Rn / Rn+1 as one 64-bit value per lane) over the executing lanes; a source value not captured -> missing_fact:axis:match_distinct_values. pytest: a synthetic MATCH record whose destination and source have different distinct counts; py == cpp segments on the corpus case. Everything else in converter_axis stands.

addenda.written: after the v5r2 data, an install / derivation audit; no new GPU run, gate rules and acceptance thresholds unchanged
addenda.text: (1) The alu5 lat harnesses k_dlat, k_lat_d64 and k_lat_f32 (and the v5 k_dlat copied from them) issue two dependent target ops per U iteration (x = op(x, y); y = op(y, x)): the SASS holds 32 DADD.RZ / DMUL.RZ / DSETP / FSETP per kernel at U = 16 on both devices (v4 builds h100-v4r1b, b300-v4s4). The v4 install took the slope over U as the per-op value, so every v4 value from these harnesses is twice the per-op latency: h100 DSETP 123.79 (= 127.79 - FSEL 4) is per op 127.79 / 2 - 4 = 59.90; FSETP 12.0 on both devices (= 16 - 4) is 16 / 2 - 4 = 4.0; h100 DADD / DMUL 128 is 64. Correction: per-op result = slope over U / 2 (then the v3 pair rule), status unchanged by the correction (pair cells experimental; DADD / DMUL from the v5 .RN cells below). The alu4 / alu5 single-op harnesses (k_lat, one op per U) are not affected. (2) model_v5 divided the dthr slope by 2 x N_unit; k_dthr issues one op per chain per K (8 chains x 16 warps = 128 warp instructions per K per SM, N_unit 128), so interval = slope / 128: h100 DADD_RN 2526.39 / 128 = 19.74, DMUL_RN 2532.35 / 128 = 19.78 (the v4 DADD_RZ value 19.558 used the same divisor). b300 dthr per-instruction 2578.58 / 128 = 20.15 < S + 2 = 66 -> unrealised:stall_bound under the nop_filler_rule as written (the rule compares the per-SM interval with one warp's stall sum; kept as frozen). (3) model_v5 dropped the dlat rows of the RN cells (no lat value); from the same data: h100 lat.DADD_RN / lat.DMUL_RN 2004 / 4052 / 8148 at U 16 / 32 / 64 (both runs), slope 128.0, residual 0 -> per-op 64.0 (measured); b300 127.87 -> 63.93 < S + 2 = 66 -> unrealised:stall_bound.
